The one-page summary of a round of discovery inside an Initiative: what we set out to learn, who we listened to, which Solutions we considered and what we decided about each. When discovery is committed for a quarter, the brief is the Deliverable.

- **Definition:** [Glossary: Discovery, Discovery brief](/system/glossary)
- **How it works:** [10 Discovery](/system/discovery)
- **Owner:** product manager
- **Links to:** Parent: [Initiative](/templates/initiative). See also: [Assumption log](/templates/assumption-log)

## Template

| Field | What goes here |
| --- | --- |
| Initiative | Name and link to the Initiative artifact |
| Outcome | The goal and the number it should move, with baseline |
| Timebox and team | Start, decision date, trio, others involved |
| Research questions | 3 to 5 questions we need answered |
| Who we listened to | Groups, how many sessions, links to notes |
| Top opportunities | 3 to 5, in users' words, with the target marked |
| Solutions considered | At least three for the target opportunity |
| Riskiest assumptions | Top three, linked to the assumption log |
| Decision | For each Solution tested: build / don't build / try something different, and why |
| Into slicing | Solution name and link, story map link, first slice |

## DMV example

**Discovery brief: Single-trip new driver licenses**

| Field | Entry |
| --- | --- |
| Initiative | Single-trip new driver licenses. "We believe repeat trips for standard new driver license applications represent an opportunity to advance Goal 2 by helping applicants know they are ready before they come in." |
| Outcome | Goal 2: zero multi-trip experiences for standard new driver licenses. Baseline: 85% of applicants need more than one trip. |
| Timebox and team | Six weeks during Q2, decision before Q3 planning. Product manager, UX designer and researcher, one developer, technical architect for feasibility, content strategist part time. |
| Research questions | What sends people home without a license? How do applicants decide what to bring? Where do staff and the website disagree? What happens between passing the knowledge test and the drive test? |
| Who we listened to | 12 sessions: 5 first-time applicants and parents of teen applicants, 4 adults new to Oregon, 3 counter staff at two field offices. One week of counter staff logging every repeat visit. |
| Top opportunities | **"I didn't know my copy wasn't good enough."** (target) / "The website and the person at the counter told me different things." / "My name doesn't match on two of my documents." / "I passed the test but had to come back for the drive test." |
| Solutions considered | A: personal document checklist. B: checklist plus document photo upload for staff review before the visit. C: real-time eligibility check at the counter. |
| Riskiest assumptions | A1, A2, A4 below |
| Decision | Checklist (A): **don't build**. Photo upload with staff review (B): **build it**. The counter log showed document problems cause 6 of 10 repeat trips. A checklist alone failed in prototype testing (A3), so staff review of uploaded photos is part of the Solution. C waits until shared identity verification can check license eligibility. The drive test scheduling gap goes to the idea log as a new Idea. |
| Into slicing | Solution: License Ready Check, in Next from Q3 planning. Story map backbone: Find out what I need, Gather documents, Check documents, Book visit, Finish at the counter. First slice: photo upload and staff review for the two most common documents. Learning slice: name mismatch cases with 20 applicants. |
